title: Normalization coupling and marker restriction in brain transcriptome inference

tables.title: Resources and analysis units
tables.note: Reference construction used four donors per internal resource; six different donors were targets. The same 15 external targets were analyzed with both references. Clinical bulk comprised 218 Alzheimer disease and 70 control samples.

tables.title: Normalization with fixed outcomes
tables.note: Direct effect 0.5 in 20 of 100 test genes. Coverage is for the 80 unaffected genes. Intervals quantify Monte Carlo uncertainty conditional on donor banks.

tables.title: Pseudocount and scale sensitivity
tables.note: All comparisons retain the same injected outcomes. The effective ratio is pseudocount divided by input scale.

tables.title: Relative-count marker perturbations
tables.note: Requested within-class fractions are 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20. Integer rounding and external annotation determine realized membership. Zero is the unperturbed control.

tables.title: Common-support calibration and precision
tables.note: Donor-equal means. Global-null power is undefined (blank). Reference-feature-matched and random means average three fixed subsets within each donor. Each unit has 50 repetitions. Donor quartiles describe heterogeneity, not confidence intervals. All interventions are feasible; test availability is separate.

tables.title: Paired common-support method contrasts
tables.note: Differences between donor-equal means on identical draws and interventions. Effects on FDR and power are probabilities; multiply by 100 for percentage points. No significance test is attached to these descriptive contrasts.

tables.title: Common-support dose retention
tables.note: Pooled count retention. The same reduced sample-by-class budget is used in both allocation rules and all seven perturbed subsets. Class indices 1-7: Astro, EndoMural, Excit, Inhib, Micro, OPC, Oligo. Blank draw counts in class rows are not applicable. Reference-feature balance is supplied as matching_balance.csv in Online Resource 3.

tables.title: Coefficient variation at direct effect 0.25
tables.note: Unperturbed internal targets; 20 affected genes. Variance components use the same 200 repetitions within gene and donor and are then averaged.

tables.title: Clinical design and estimability
tables.note: 288 donors; 218 AD and 70 controls. All models share the fixed outcome matrix and the same 16,161-gene BH family.

tables.title: Clinical coefficient and discovery stability
tables.note: Each method is compared with TMM under the same reference. Threshold crossings count gained plus lost discoveries. Standard-error ratios and coefficient-weight distances are reported for MRN. Blank weight distances for other methods were not evaluated. Eq. (S4) checks the weight identity.

tables.title: Donor-level clinical marker associations
tables.note: GSE174367, primary age-, sex- and batch-adjusted owner-class analyses. Fold-change counts are descriptive point estimates. Planned-family multiplicity correction spans both panels and all seven classes.

tables.title: Actual-span reporting diagnostics
tables.note: The same MEAD point predictions enter both reporting rules. HC3 inference concerns expression coefficients. Full-six requires six composition contrasts; actual-span uses the observed nuisance rank.

tables.title: Fixed-response clinical perturbations
tables.note: Only tested-gene counts in AD samples are multiplied by exp(log_count_step) for composition-input construction; responses remain fixed. Threshold crossings measure sensitivity, not false positives.

tables.title: Local diagnostic qualification
tables.note: Post-hoc reliability audit of previously held-out scores. Derivative agreement must be at most 0.1; numerical invariance floor is 1e-6. Qualified scores all equal zero after flooring. Performance is available in Online Resource 3.

tables.title: Clinical derivative-step checks
tables.note: Central differences compared at h and h/2. Agreement above 0.1 signals an unstable local approximation. Finite perturbations in Table S13 do not rely on a derivative approximation.

tables.title: Fixed-response cross-estimator comparison
tables.note: Four reference-target settings and 42 units; 20 repetitions per unit and two outcome effects. Four observed reference donors remain fixed. Each method uses identical mixtures, outcomes and the full 100-gene BH family across probes. Coverage spans all available genes. Means weight donors equally; mc_se is conditional Monte Carlo uncertainty, not donor-population uncertainty. Power is undefined under the global null. Baseline contrasts are blank. The maximum columns span all datasets in the setting.
